A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SS-NO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original PDE benchmark experiments, architectural ablations and learned-damping analyses in Section 6 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v5 retains original experiments and adds higher-resolution evaluations, computational-cost measurements, spherical shallow-water forecasting and AirfRANS results.

M1.justification: The core spatial/temporal S4 architecture, objective and pseudocode remain unchanged. Appendix J adds task-specific adaptations using learned coordinate transformations for spherical data and replacing Transolver attention with SS-NO for AirfRANS. Mamba and graph-based backbones remain proposed future extensions.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds spherical shallow-water forecasting and AirfRANS aerodynamic field/coefficient prediction, extending evaluation to curved domains and irregular meshes. The original Burgers, KS, Navier–Stokes and Euler coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v5 adds Spherical FNO and Transolver as evaluated comparators in Tables 7 and 8. The comparator sets in the retained benchmark and ablation experiments remain unchanged; the revised FNO Fourier-mode setting is a protocol change.

E3.justification: KS evaluation expands to spatial resolutions 256 and 512. Appendix E.3 changes TorusLi FNO from the previously specified full-mode setting to eight modes. New protocols include batch-one inference benchmarking, SWE training over 10 steps with evaluation through step 100, and AirfRANS field and coefficient metrics.

E4.justification: v5 adds extended resolution-sensitivity analysis, runtime/FLOP versus accuracy comparisons, SWE long-rollout stability evaluation and a reported comparison of TorusLi FNO mode counts. The existing damping, directionality, context, memory-window, teacher-forcing and factorization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Main accuracy results still use five independent seeded runs. Section 5.3 replaces the single 1D variability bound with resolution-specific bounds, and Appendix H introduces latency averaging over 100 post-warmup iterations. No increase in training-run counts is stated.

E6.justification: v5 adds high-resolution KS curves, computational costs and SWE/AirfRANS outcomes. TorusLi FNO2D error changes from 0.0760 to 0.0452 under the revised mode setting, while SS-NO remains 0.0345. Table 7 reports step-100 errors of 2.82 for SFNO and 1.28 for SS-NO; Table 8 reports better SS-NO field errors but worse lift error than Transolver.

T1.justification: Appendix B broadens the formal full-field-of-view condition from an everywhere-nonzero iterated kernel to full support and revises the associated proof argument. New Appendix I supplies a constructive FNO-kernel recovery derivation using zero damping, harmonic frequencies and rank-one decompositions of spectral weight matrices.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow state-of-the-art assertions to strong or competitive performance, while Section 6.2 specifies superiority among evaluated methods. The central universality, FNO-recovery, adaptive-damping and parameter-efficiency contributions remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations of resolution saturation, computational overhead and geometric adaptation. Appendices J–M explicitly discuss directional scanning's lack of equivariance and hypothesize that the LTI backbone explains the AirfRANS lift deficit. These substantially expand v2's more general cautions about memory costs and irregular domains.

D1.justification: Appendix H documents an NVIDIA A6000, batch size one, thop profiling with custom spectral handlers and GPU warmup. Appendix E.3 documents the eight-mode TorusLi exception. Existing training recipes, pseudocode and access links largely remain; the new geometric adaptations receive limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to AirfRANS, Geo-FNO, Transolver, Hydra, Graph-Mamba and pLSTM, positioning them as datasets, adaptation frameworks or possible future backbones. The main related-work discussion and positioning relative to FNO, SSMs and MemNO remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained. Changes include targeted abstract and KS-discussion rewrites, expanded proof explanations, a MemNO background appendix, and separate limitations and future-work sections.

P2.justification: v2's detailed 1D benchmark table is replaced by v5's four-panel resolution plot. Damping figures are regrouped, and a new cost-accuracy figure and three new experimental tables are added. Existing architecture and supplementary-ablation graphics are retained, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The cost measurements and explicit FNO-recovery derivation strengthen support for central claims, while the revised TorusLi comparison and narrower headline claims improve calibration. These gains are tempered by sparse SWE/AirfRANS reproducibility details, loss of the exact 1D comparison table, and an unchanged FNO2D parameter count that is not reconciled with the new eight-mode exception.
